clue.text: Age Concern is pressured to give pledge

indicators.note: letters put under pressure are squeezed out of shape, so these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A charity for the elderly is being leaned on to make a promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressured' rearranges the twelve letters of AGE CONCERN IS. Age Concern was a British charity for older people.
explanation.definitionFit: A recognisance is a formal bond or undertaking given to a court, a kind of legal promise.

clue.text: Harvester retains power to decorate again

indicators.note: the harvesting word keeps another piece held within it

parts.note: a reaper is one who harvests crops
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A farm machine keeps its engine for redecorating.
explanation.definitionFit: To repaper a room is to hang fresh wallpaper, decorating it once more.

clue.text: Original type of race rerouted over hill

indicators.note: in a down answer the scrambled piece sits over, above, the hill
sent along a different route, so the letters of race take a new order

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, common in Dartmoor place names

explanation.surface: A distinctive sort of running race diverted across a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A creator is an originator, someone of the original sort who makes a thing first.

clue.text: Sluggish type, after talk, walked to secure work

indicators.note: the walking piece follows on after the talk piece

parts.note: gas is idle chatter

indicators.note: the walking word holds the work piece fast inside it

parts.note: trod is the past tense of tread, to walk
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A lazy person, after a chat, strolled off to get a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sluggish type' reads as a lazy person, but it means a creature of the slug kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Slugs and snails belong to the class of molluscs called gastropods.

clue.text: Get used to old rail union that is taking over

indicators.note: the abbreviation takes the union into its middle, absorbing it

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, a former British trade union

explanation.surface: Become accustomed to a former railway union that is in charge now.
explanation.definitionFit: To inure is to accustom or harden someone to something unpleasant.

clue.text: Material state in Paris limited by expert

indicators.note: the French word is bounded on either side by the expert word

parts.note: an ace is someone highly skilled
etat is French for state

explanation.surface: A fabric shown in a French state, constrained by a specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetate is a synthetic fibre and fabric made from cellulose.

clue.text: Fall of bounder caught by police investigation

indicators.note: the bounder piece is trapped inside the investigation piece

parts.note: a case is a matter the police investigate
a cad is a dishonourable man, an old British sense of bounder

explanation.surface: A rogue's downfall after being nabbed by detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a waterfall, water falling in stages.

clue.text: Favouring private eye with time to speak of Cromwell's state

parts.note: pro means in favour of
tec is short for detective
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: Supporting a detective who takes time to talk about a Puritan leader's government.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Cromwell ruled England as Lord Protector from 1653, so his regime is named after that title.
explanation.definitionFit: The Protectorate was the English republic governed by Cromwell as Lord Protector, 1653 to 1659.

clue.text: Check traveller on ship

parts.note: a rep, or commercial traveller, is a travelling salesman
re means on or concerning
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: Stop a voyager on board a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress is to hold back or restrain, as when checking an urge.

clue.text: Use lint for wrapping up handy tool

indicators.note: bundling the words up together jumbles them, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to dress a wound with lint, a convenient tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for wrapping up' looks like the purpose of the lint, but 'wrapping up' rearranges USE LINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is an implement, especially a kitchen one, kept close by for use.

clue.text: They check pork pies in East London

definitions.text: They check pork pies in East London

parts.words: They check pork pies in East London
parts.note: pork pies is Cockney rhyming slang for lies, so these are devices that test whether someone is telling falsehoods

explanation.surface: Food inspectors examining pastries in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang, spoken in East London, 'pork pies' (or 'porkies') means lies.
explanation.definitionFit: A polygraph measures bodily signs to judge whether a speaker is being truthful.

clue.text: One advising of attempt to attract attention in row

indicators.note: the attention sound goes inside the row word

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
pst is the hissed sound used to catch someone's notice

explanation.surface: An adviser hissing to get noticed from among the seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipster gives tips, advice on betting or investments.

clue.text: Give out an appellation about note

indicators.note: turned about, so the article and the name are read backwards together

parts.note: an appellation is a name
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Announce a title concerning a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns A NAME into EMANA, then TE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source.

clue.text: Nurse has un-English vocation

indicators.note: the E, for English, is removed from the profession word

parts.note: a career is a calling or profession

explanation.surface: A nurse has a calling not suited to England.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer looks after someone sick or disabled, much as a nurse tends patients.

clue.text: Hold on for a cut by Spain

parts.note: per means for each, as in per head
to sever is to cut
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Keep going for a haircut beside Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to keep at something despite difficulty, refusing to give up.

clue.text: Supernumerary Communist and German worker

parts.note: red is a common label for a communist
und is German for and
a worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: An extra Communist and a German labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something redundant is surplus to requirements, beyond the number needed.

clue.text: Not liking well-endowed shed

parts.note: to be off something is to have gone off it
loaded means very wealthy

explanation.surface: Cooling on a wealthy person who has been cast aside.
explanation.definitionFit: To offload is to unload or get rid of something, as when shedding a burden.

clue.text: Opening of clenched hand united the French

parts.note: a fist is a tightly closed hand
la is French for the (feminine)

explanation.surface: A fist's opening when the French come together.
explanation.definitionFit: A fistula is an abnormal passage or opening between organs in medicine.

clue.text: Alfresco broadcasting covers Physical Education

indicators.note: the broadcasting phrase wraps around the education letters

parts.note: on air means currently being broadcast

explanation.surface: An outdoor broadcast featuring PE lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' puts PE inside ON AIR, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfresco, from Italian, means outdoors, in the fresh air.

clue.text: Is to take legal action in disputed question

parts.note: to sue is to bring a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Whether to go to court is a contested matter.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a point in dispute, a matter under debate.

clue.text: Almost offend a king, being narrow in outlook

indicators.note: nearly all of the word, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: to insult is to offend
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Nearly insulting a monarch with small-minded views.
explanation.definitionFit: Insular describes islanders cut off from others, hence parochial, closed to wider ideas.

clue.text: Lieutenant in steep refuge

indicators.note: the officer abbreviation goes inside the steepness word

parts.note: sheer describes a very steep slope

explanation.surface: An army officer sheltering on a sheer slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter is a place of safety or protection, a haven.

clue.text: A woman holding science can produce a carbuncle

indicators.note: the woman's name holds the science abbreviation inside it

parts.note: Bess is a woman's name, short for Elizabeth
Sc is an abbreviation for science, as in BSc

explanation.surface: A female scientist manages to grow a boil.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle is a cluster of boils, a pus-filled swelling like this one.

clue.text: Scandinavian gets married in Kent?

indicators.note: the married word sits inside the region letters

parts.note: Kent is a county in South East England, abbreviated SE
wed means married

explanation.surface: A Nordic person marries in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in the south-east of England, so it stands for SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swede is a native of Sweden, one of the Scandinavian countries.

clue.text: New climb which is just coming into being

parts.note: an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: A fresh ascent that is only just beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means emerging, beginning to exist or develop.

clue.text: Copy fast runner no more

parts.note: the emu is a flightless bird that runs swiftly
late means dead, no longer living

explanation.surface: Imitate a speedy athlete who has passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate is to imitate someone, matching or rivalling them.

clue.text: No cloud no moon and no extras?

definitions.text: No cloud no moon and no extras?

parts.words: No cloud no moon and no extras?
parts.note: a clear moonless sky is full of nothing but stellar points, and a cast with no extras has only top names

explanation.surface: A night with clear skies, and a film with no crowd scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: A cloudless, moonless sky shows only stars; a film or team without extras is made up entirely of big names.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-star cast or team is made up wholly of famous performers.

clue.text: Quack remedy for the distressed?

parts.note: distressed is read as dis-tressed, having lost one's tresses, and the quack remedy is a dubious tonic for the bald

explanation.surface: A charlatan's cure for people in anguish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' looks like upset, but read as dis-tressed it means bald, without tresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Such products are lotions sold with dubious claims to regrow lost locks on a balding scalp.
